predecessors.name: Kalinga
predecessors.text: Kalinga, 'an ancient ruling dynasty of Kalinga after the decline of the Maurya Empire'

successors.name: Gupta Empire
successors.text: Odisha, the Kalinga core; the infobox lists the Kushan Empire, the Murunda dynasty and the Gupta Empire as successors

ledger.x: c. 170 BCE: the Mahameghavahana take Kalinga. The page: 'an ancient ruling dynasty of Kalinga after the decline of the Maurya Empire', 'Established: 2nd or 1st century BC', its regnal list opening with Mahameghavahana (founder) 140 BCE; the Kalinga infobox gives 170 BCE. -170 is Cliopatria's year and the kalinga…

c. 50 BCE: Kharavela's dynasty holds Kosala. 'In the first century B.C. conquered Kalinga and Kosala'; 'The third ruler of the dynasty, Khārabēḷa, conquered much of India in a series of campaigns'; the infobox lists Kharavela at 50 BCE. The page names no state in Kosala.
ledger.cp: South Kosala (no state named on the page)

ledger.x: early 2nd century CE: the Satavahanas take South Kosala.
4th century CE: the dynasty is gone.

wars.name: Kharavela's campaigns
wars.outcome: Kharavela 'led many successful campaigns against the states of Magadha, Anga, the Satavahanas' and 'attacked Rajagriha in Magadha, thus inducing the Indo-Greek king Demetrius I of Bactria to retreat to Mathura'; in year 2 he sent an army west against…

wars.name: Gautamiputra Satakarni's conquest of South Kosala
wars.outcome: 'South Kosala was later conquered by Gautamiputra Satakarni of the Satavahana dynasty' in the early 2nd century CE.

certainty.note: A dynasty known from the Hathigumpha and Mancapuri inscriptions and its regnal list; no frontier is dated, and the extent claims of Kharavela are contested.
